title: Matched contextual influence and observable-rationale monitoring

source.paper: Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Can Be Unreliable in Implicit-Influence Settings
source.adaptation: Small binary-choice adaptation of Setting 1; not a full reproduction

hypothesis: A contextual detail delivered as a casual aside may shift a model's choice while its short returned rationale does not attribute the choice to that detail as often as an explicit instruction does.
competingExplanation: Any apparent shift may reflect ordinary stochastic variation, prompt salience, or a direct preference cue rather than implicit influence, and any monitor difference may reflect rationale length or judge behavior.
falsifier: If held-out implicit and explicit conditions have similar target-aligned choice rates and similar observable-rationale detection among shifted trials, this pilot does not support the hypothesized delivery gap.
independentVariable: delivery of the same contextual detail: baseline, implicit aside, explicit instruction, plus neutral and relevant positive controls
primaryOutcome: target-aligned choice rate by condition, compared descriptively for implicit versus explicit delivery on held-out cases
secondaryOutcome: monitor YES rate among trials whose choice switched from the per-case baseline majority

controls.neutral: irrelevant color preference should not change the choice
controls.relevantPositive: directly relevant lower cost should increase target-aligned choices, validating choice parsing

taskSet.independentUnit: case-by-seed trial pair; this is an exploratory pilot, not a population estimate

model.access: OpenRouter returns message content and usage metadata; the provider may also report reasoning token counts, which are not requested or stored as evidence

analysis.choice: majority baseline per case, then count target-aligned and baseline-switching outputs by condition
analysis.uncertainty: Wilson 95% intervals are shown for monitor rates when a denominator exists; the small number of cases and repeated calls make this descriptive only
analysis.missing: failed or unparsable trials stay in raw evidence and are excluded from the corresponding completed-output denominator
analysis.stoppingRule: stop before the reserved $1 calibration cap, at 120 calls, after two consecutive provider failures, or after planned trials complete

budget.estimate: under $0.15 at current catalog rates for the planned 70 subject/monitor calls, assuming short responses; actual provider usage is authoritative
budget.reservation: runner checks a hard call ceiling and records provider-returned cost per response
budget.otherProviders: no OpenAI API or Exa spend is part of this experiment contract

limits: This is a bounded adaptation and cannot reproduce the paper's seven-model, four-setting benchmark.
A short returned rationale is observable explanation, not hidden chain-of-thought.
Two held-out cases cannot establish a general model or deployment property.
The endpoint, routing, and model behavior may change over time.
Monitor judgments are model-generated and not independently human validated in this pilot.
